_meta.field_note: DESIGN_RULES section 4 requires id, site, category, prompt, answer spec, check type, authored, trigger note. start_url, tolerance, verification, stability, risks, pilot_logging are additions for the reporting commitments (section 8); trim if unwanted.

check_semantics.normalize: fold thousands separators ONLY via (\d),(\d{3})(?!\d) -> digits (leaves comma-separated lists like '8135,8324,8454,8569' intact); remove currency tokens ($, US$, USD); map U+2212 and dash variants used as signs to '-'; map the word-signs 'negative <num>' / 'minus <num>' to '-<num>'; matching case-insensitive. Normalize runs BEFORE set extraction too.
check_semantics.candidates: boundary-aware regex matches of the task's gold pattern plus each listed distractor; a band distractor matches any standalone number in [lo,hi] other than the gold. Text spans matched by the gold pattern are NEVER distractor candidates (e.g. the 'iq3_m' inside T2-2's gold filename does not trigger the quant-token distractor).
check_semantics.exemption_negation: a negation/contrast marker (not, n't, never, wrong, incorrect, rather than, instead of, excluding) drops ONLY THE NEXT candidate, at distance marker-end to candidate-start <= 25 chars, and only if no clause break (comma, semicolon, period, dash, 'but') and no other candidate intervenes. So 'the answer is NOT 32037' fails (gold dropped); 'not 32038 but 32037' passes (32038 dropped, clause break protects the gold); 'I'm not sure, but 32037' passes (clause break intervenes).
check_semantics.exemption_attribution: attribution tokens are listed PER DISTRACTOR VALUE in each task, matched at word boundaries ('male' does not match inside 'female'), with a BIDIRECTIONAL window of 12 chars between token edge and candidate edge; a matched attribution drops that distractor candidate only.
check_semantics.verdict: PASS iff at least one gold candidate survives and the LAST surviving candidate in the final answer is the gold. Gold-presence tasks (T2-3) mean UNNEGATED presence. FAIL records which distractor (if any) was the final assertion - feeds failure classification.
check_semantics.set_match: set-check tasks use their stated extraction rule on the NORMALIZED answer; PASS iff the extracted set exactly equals ONE of the listed gold sets (no extras, no mixtures).
check_semantics.provenance: v3, 2026-07-09: adopted after a second independent verification pass broke the original hand-written T1-3r clause in both directions; refined the same day after a third adversarial pass found 12 further defects (T4-1 proximity pool broken both directions, T3-2 extraction counting the 'I found 4 issues' count, comma-normalize fusing comma-separated set answers, unbound negation windows killing 'not 32038 but 32037', trailing explanatory mentions false-failing diligent answers, spec ambiguities that flipped this file's own worked examples). The checker implements THIS block and must pass _meta.test_vectors before any pilot run is scored. v3.1, 2026-07-10: fourth pass added the T4-1 bare-number fallback and the plural-aware males? attribution token; vectors 28-30. v4, 2026-07-11: decimal/dual golds and url_gate added for the generation-2 chained T1 tasks; the retired tasks' nine vectors left with their tasks; gen-2 vectors appended. The checker must pass the full list before any pilot run is scored. Round-3 red-team of the gen-2 rules (2026-07-11, independent agent, all findings execution-confirmed): 6 trailing-context false-fails -> token lists widened; Dec*/Sep* overbreadth -> anchored; url-gate substring matching -> structural host/path/i-param parsing with word-boundary tokens; topic must_any lists widened. Attack strings frozen below; 50/50 green.
check_semantics.decimal_golds: gen-2 tasks may list DECIMAL gold literals, matched boundary-aware after normalization (no digit or '.' adjacent): e.g. 8.1/8.10; DUAL golds 17.3/17.1 (the pod may show the December value, the annual average, or both - any listed gold is gold); 1.91/1.9/1.90. Distractors on decimal tasks are ENUMERATED literals only - no band rules - so verbatim source phrasing ('rose 10.4 percentage points') can never become a candidate. Attribution and negation rules apply unchanged; last-assertion verdict unchanged.
check_semantics.url_gate: tasks with check_type 'string_match + url_gate' additionally require: at least one steps.jsonl URL (url_before/url_after, any step at or before the answer step) whose PARSED host is wolframalpha.com (or a subdomain) AND path starts with '/input' AND whose decoded i= query parameter word-boundary-matches ALL tokens in query_must_all and AT LEAST ONE in query_must_any (per-task lists in the tolerance field; topic lists widened 2026-07-11: unemployment/unemployed/jobless; cpi/consumer price/price index/cost of living; inflation/cpi/consumer price - the CPI-YoY phrasing IS the gold convention for T1-3c). Structural parsing is load-bearing (red-team 2026-07-11): substring matching wrongly passed a '1923' inside a timestamp param on a 1924 query, and a duckduckgo URL that merely mentioned wolframalpha. Gate failure -> verdict FAIL, final_assertion 'url-gate', with the string verdict preserved under string_result for the failure rubric. urls=None -> url_gate 'not_evaluated' (scoring runs MUST supply urls); urls=[] (empty log, e.g. crashed run) FAILS the gate - crashed runs classify under the rubric before scoring.

tasks.tolerance: check_semantics v4 instantiation - golds: literals 8.1 / 8.10 (boundary-aware; '%', 'percent', bare number all fine). Enumerated distractors with attribution tokens (bidirectional 12-char window, word-boundary): 14.8 and 14.7 [April, peak*, high, spring, reach*, pandemic, rose, ris*, month*] (the April peak; 14.7 is the as-first-published figure, revised to 14.8), 6.7 [Dec(ember), Nov(ember), end*, month*], 13.2 [May, month*], 11.0 [June, month*], 10.2 [July, month*], 8.4 [August, Aug, month*], 7.8 [September, Sep*, month*], 6.9 [October, Oct, month*], 4.4 [March, month*], 3.6 [Jan(uary), month*, prev-year tokens], 3.5 [February, Feb, month*], 3.7 [2019, previous, prior, earlier, year before], 5.3 / 5.4 [2021, following, next]. NO band rule - only enumerated values are candidates, so verbatim BLS phrasing ('rose 10.4 percentage points') cannot false-fail. Last-assertion verdict. URL GATE (success-gating, Frank's decision 2026-07-11): a WA /input URL whose decoded query contains '2020' AND 'unemployment' must appear in or before the answer step, else FAIL ('url-gate') regardless of the answer string - this is what makes 'the final read is on a rendered surface' true against memorization. TOKEN LISTS WIDENED 2026-07-11 after the gen-2 red-team (round 3): trailing-context narration ('up from 3.7% a year earlier', 'ending the year at 6.7%', 'reached 14.8 in the spring', 'falling to 5.4% the following year') must exempt its value or correct verbose answers false-fail; month abbreviations anchored (Dec(ember), Sep(t)(ember)) so 'declined'/'separate' cannot exempt an asserted distractor. Residual accepted+logged: attribution can exempt an ASSERTED distractor when gold is also mentioned ('the December figure, 6.7%, is the answer') - requires misreading the prompt while citing gold; and a non-enumerated wrong value ('WA shows 2.0%') cannot be the final assertion - both same-class as pre-accepted harsh modes, review under check-artifact.

GEN-2 (2026-07-11): prompt de-prescribed and a locate hop added - start_url moved to the HF homepage, so the agent must first find the bartowski repo among look-alikes (43 repos named exactly '<org>/Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct-GGUF' as of 2026-07-11). This kills result counts ('I found 4 issues'), days-of-month, and list ordinals without touching the gold range. Belt-and-braces: ISO dates and month-name+year phrases stripped first. tasks.prompt: On Coursera, find the course titled 'Wind Energy' offered by the Technical University of Denmark (DTU) and report how many modules it contains.
tasks.tolerance: check_semantics instantiation - candidates are numbers SYNTACTICALLY BOUND to 'module(s)' (v3; replaces the broken 30-char proximity pool, which false-passed '15 modules (16 weeks)' and false-failed '16 modules ... 39 hours'): a number (digits or 'sixteen') is a candidate iff it matches (num)\s+(?:\w+\s+)?modules?\b or modules?\s*[:\-]?\s*(num); numbers bound to another unit noun (hours?, weeks?, minutes?, stars?, ratings?) are never candidates. Gold: 16. Last-assertion rule applies within the candidate pool. v3.1 fallback (fourth verification pass): if the answer contains NO module-bound number at all and exactly one standalone number not bound to another unit noun, that number is the candidate - so a bare '16' passes while '16 weeks' still fails.

tasks.prompt: On Apple's online store, find the starting ('From') price for a 13-inch MacBook Air in Sky Blue with the chip option that has the 10-core GPU.
tasks.tolerance: check_semantics instantiation - gold: (?<!\d)1399(?:\.00)?(?!\d) after normalization (covers $1,399 / 'From $1399' / 1399.00 USD; boundary anchors added 2026-07-09 so digit-runs like 13990 cannot false-pass). Distractors: (?<!\d)1299(?:\.00)?(?!\d) [8-core-GPU state] and (?<!\d)1499(?:\.00)?(?!\d) [15-inch state], negation/contrast exemption applies ('$1,399, not the $1,299 8-core option' passes). If gold is absent, record which distractor was the final assertion. Attribution tokens (added v3): '8-core' scoped to 1299 and '15-inch' scoped to 1499 - trailing comparisons ('$1,399 - $100 more than the $1,299 8-core config') pass; 'more than' alone is not a negation marker and does not exempt.
tasks.trigger_note: T4 three-dimension picker: large size tiles (13"/15"), circular color swatches (Sky Blue/Silver/Starlight/Midnight), large chip tiles ('10-core CPU, 8-core GPU' vs '10-core CPU, 10-core GPU'). Verified: the page JSON has NO preselected dimension, so the agent must actively select all three before the target 'From' price renders — the displayed price is selection-state-dependent, and confirming which tile/swatch is highlighted (a visual ring) before reading the price is a real hidden-state moment. Selected state also exposed via aria-checked, so opt-in is plausible rather than forced — correct for T4. Price is identical across colors within a size/chip combo, so a color-swatch mistake cannot corrupt the answer. GEN-2 (2026-07-11): prompt de-prescribed (no buy-page URL, no tile-by-tile instructions - the three selections are implied by the requested configuration) and a storefront hop added (start at apple.com, navigate to the MacBook Air configurator).
tasks.verification: 2026-07-08: curled the page (200, 563KB, no bot wall — pilot-relevant for this pilot-gated site) and parsed the embedded price JSON: 13inch-skyblue-10-10 -> 'From $1399'; distractors confirmed (13inch-*-10-8 -> $1299; 15inch -> $1499). Cross-checked via a second rendered fetch.
tasks.stability: M5-generation lineup early in its cycle; Apple mid-cycle price changes are rare. Re-pin at run time if Apple refreshes the Air.
tasks.risks: Shortcut fails safe: pre-M5 memory anchors on M4-era prices ($999/$1,199) which FAIL the check. The embedded JSON contains all prices, but browser-use extraction surfaces rendered content, not script-tag JSON. NO LOGIN, NO BAG/CHECKOUT: the task ends at reading the price; never proceed past the configurator.

tasks.prompt: According to the population pyramid of Japan in 2026 shown in the English Wikipedia article 'Demographics of Japan', what percentage of the total population are females aged 75-79?
tasks.tolerance: check_semantics instantiation - gold: (?<![\d.])3\.9(?:0)?(?!\d) (trailing zero accepted), EXCLUDING any match followed within 2 tokens by a millions marker (million, M, mn - guards the article table's 3,953,000 count collision in all abbreviations; the question asks a percentage). Distractors with attribution tokens (word-boundary matched, bidirectional 12-char window): 3.3 [tokens: males?], 3.1 / 3.2 / 5.68 / 7.22 [tokens: table, comput*, calculat*, cohort, 'both sexes'], 4.0 / 4% [tokens: 50-54, largest]. Verified behaviors: 'the table computes ~3.2 but the pyramid shows 3.9%' PASSES; 'female 3.9%, male 3.3%' PASSES ('male' at word boundary cannot match inside 'female'); 'Females 75-79 are 3.9% (the whole cohort is 5.68%)' PASSES; bare table-derived '3.2%' FAILS; '3.9M women' FAILS; swapped 'male: 3.9%, female: 3.3%' FAILS (3.3 unexempted, last).
tasks.trigger_note: P0 positive control (instrument validation only; excluded from the success comparison pool by pre-commitment). The per-sex percentage labels exist ONLY in the pyramid PNG pixels: the has no alt attribute; the caption is exactly 'Population pyramid of Japan in 2026' (no data); '3.9%' occurs zero times in page HTML (visible-text '3.9' zero times after tag-stripping; embedded chart data like '[1907,13.9]' cannot match); the Commons file page is also pixels-only (its only '3.9' hits are parser-profiling comments). The article's own DOM age table computes to ~3.1-3.2% — a DIFFERENT value — so a DOM-derived answer is wrong by construction; only reading the rendered bars yields 3.9. GEN-2 (2026-07-11): prompt compressed to the what-only form; still names the pyramid as the authoritative artifact (necessary - the article's own table computes a conflicting ~3.2, so without the artifact pin the table answer would be a fair reading and the control ambiguous).
tasks.verification: 2026-07-08: downloaded the PNG (Commons Special:FilePath/Japan_population_pyramid_2026.png, 1876x1324) and read it visually — female 75-79 bar labeled 3.9% (male 3.3%; largest bars 50-54 at 4%/4.0%); reviewer independently repeated both the image read and the negative greps. Table row 75-79 confirmed: 3,193,000 male / 3,953,000 female / 5.68 both-sexes share.
tasks.stability: Image authored for 2026, captioned '...in 2026'; annual-update pattern suggests replacement ~January 2027. Re-check via one Commons GET before the run (file overwrite is the main risk).
tasks.risks: Vision-arm practical note: the 330px infobox thumbnail is unreadable — the agent must click through to the file page or full resolution (1-3 extra steps, still <12; makes the hidden-state moment two-staged: notice image, then enlarge). A DOM-arm agent answering from parametric memory could land near 3.8-4.0 (dankai cohort estimate); nearest guesses 4.0 and 3.3 are rejected, and 3 repeats per cell expose memory-luck as inconsistency. Classify DOM-arm failures here as 'DOM-blind' (expected), not agent-limited.
tasks.pilot_logging: If the DOM arm PASSES this task consistently, the positive control is compromised (parametric leakage) — swap in backup pilot-P0-1 (arXiv 2312.10997v5 Figure 2).
